critiques.summary: Read the projection writer, the extension reader, the tree model and both test suites over the repo, plus verification_stamp, gate_checks, run_of_record, the watcher registration and the UAT walk. Five Major findings, all confirmed and fixed in the same session: the group row could paint the done glyph on an undecided close, the volatility classification missed two stamp/digest-backed checks, a damaged payload degraded to an empty confident list, the file watcher did not cover the projection so the row would not move after the command the UAT walk prescribes, and the reader's dirent check diverged from the writer's os.path.isfile on symlinks.

findings.description: closeOutGlyph counted only unmet rows, so an all-met report whose verdict is `undecided-backstop-would-route` (would_close: null, a routed round still standing) rendered `nothing outstanding` with done.svg. Fixed: the glyph requires fresh + zero outstanding + verdict `would-close`, the summary names the undecided case, and an all-clear is always dated.

The volatility rule was derived from a source-text scan for a direct `_run_git` call, which is blind to how `verification_integrity` (evidence stamp binding the repo-wide work diff) and `test_run_fresh` (run_of_record freshness digest over covered source) depend on the repository. Editing a module outside the session-set directory changed both answers while the tree read `fresh`. Fixed by inverting the default: SET_LOCAL_CHECKS names the set-local checks and everything else is volatile, guarded by an AST walk that follows function-local imports.

A parseable version-1 payload with a missing or non-array `report.obligations`, or with malformed rows, read as `fresh` with an empty obligation list — which the tree then rendered as `nothing outstanding`. Non-ENOENT read failures were also classified as `absent`. Fixed: any structural damage is `unreadable`, and only ENOENT is `absent`.

The session-set file watcher's glob did not include close-obligations.json, so after running the prescribed `close_preflight --write` the panel would not move until the 30-second poll — the one moment the operator is watching that row on purpose, and exactly what the UAT walk tells them to do. Fixed by adding it to the existing watcher pattern (and to the D1 watcher-inventory allowlist).

The reader used `readdirSync({ withFileTypes: true })` + `entry.isFile()`, which reports false for a symlink to a regular file, while the writer's `os.path.isfile` follows it. One symlinked artifact in a session set would make the key sets differ permanently and pin the panel at `stale`. Fixed with statSync, plus a runtime test and a structural guard (Layer 2 is skipped in CI and unprivileged Windows cannot create symlinks, so the structural one is what always runs).

critiques.summary: Independently read close_preflight.py, the extension reader and tree model, both step-model files, the new tests, gate_checks, verification_stamp and run_of_record with repo access. Two Major findings, both fixed: the volatility classification missed the transitively git-backed checks (verification_integrity, test_run_fresh, verification_backstop), and the TypeScript reader's dirent-based file test diverges from Python's os.path.isfile for symlinks. The two findings were reached independently of the other provider's pass and converge with two of its five.

findings.description: GIT_BACKED_CHECKS omitted the checks that reach git transitively — verification_integrity and test_run_fresh through compute_work_diff_sha256 / surface_digest, and the backstop through both — because the derivation test only text-matched `_run_git` inside each top-level check function. Those rows therefore rendered as re-checkable truth in a projection the tree called fresh, hiding blocking failures and the backstop cost warning until the operator tried to close.

Python's os.path.isfile returns true for a symlink to a file; TypeScript's Dirent.isFile() returns false. A session set holding a symlinked artifact would be digested differently by writer and reader, the key sets would never match, and the Work Explorer would report the projection stale forever with no operator remedy.
